reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the presenter promotes Bitclub Network with a mining-share purchase offer and registration prompt, while claiming daily Bitcoin withdrawals and passive income. The presenter also describes entering a withdrawal and providing a wallet address and PIN, though the displayed records do not independently verify the transaction or broader earnings claims. The description links to a separate cryptocurrency-earning site, but the speaker's reference to viewers' time and $50 has unclear payment conditions and relationship to that destination.

citations.quote: And here I just add a sum amount of 2.1 bitcoin.

opening.argument: Judge the video by the limits it actually communicates. The withdrawal page warns that requests may take up to 24 hours and that withdrawals below 2 Bitcoin incur a fee [F0018]. The presenter treats account access as a security concern, explaining that the authorization code is one-time [ASR_0002]. He also proposes watching how long this particular transaction takes, rather than promising every request will settle on the same schedule [ASR_0001]. Those qualifications matter: a demonstration with stated fees, processing time and account safeguards should not be read as an unconditional promise of fast, cost-free returns.

citations.quote: This pin code is a one-off code. It can protect your office from the variousutabled access to your home.
last transaction I had took place in four hours look how long this transaction will go

rebuttal.rebuttal: The mining-share offer and registration prompt show promotion [F0012], but promotion does not erase the withdrawal conditions displayed elsewhere [F0018]. Nor does a wallet record prove that the presenter secretly guarantees future earnings: the prosecution itself says the records do not independently verify the transaction. The uncertain meaning of his final $50 remark cannot establish a definite payment demand [ASR_0002].

citations.quote: And that is all I need your time and money at $50.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A processing-time warning and one-time PIN concern do not qualify the central earnings pitch. The video displays a $1,000 GPU-pool share purchase offer [F0012], repeatedly directs viewers to register through the link below [F0001], and shows commissions attributed to members in the account holder's team [F0058]. The presenter also calls the next payment a fee for passive income due in 20 hours [ASR_0002]. None of the cited cautions establishes that buying shares or joining the promoted network is safe.

citations.quote: the next fee for passive income as I had just mentioned is in just 20 hours everyday

opening.argument: The sustained activity here is a walkthrough of a Bitcoin withdrawal. The presenter says a wallet address must be specified before withdrawing [ASR_0001], then explains the choice between an emailed PIN and a Google authorization code [ASR_0002]. The screen shows a withdrawal form with a security-code field [F0030], followed by a transaction-history view listing the request as pending [F0041]. A judge can recognize promotional context without turning every step of an operational demonstration into an instruction to invest. The shown sequence chiefly teaches viewers what the account workflow looks like; it does not independently establish what anyone else will earn.

citations.quote: Before withdrawing, it is necessary to specify the address of your wallet that you have in this bank and press the SAFE BTC button.
I will use the pin code of Google authorization installed in my office.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution points to the share offer and registration banner [F0012], but those are context around a sequence devoted to entering a withdrawal and checking its status [F0030][F0041]. Its own caution that the records do not independently verify the transaction is appropriate; it also means the walkthrough should not be treated as proof of earnings. The external description offers a place to learn about cryptocurrency earning [DESCRIPTION_0001], without showing what that destination contains.

citations.quote: learn how to earn in cryptocurrency safely and easily without trading on exchanges and large ...

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The withdrawal steps are real, but they are embedded in a pitch, not isolated instruction. The page offers GPU mining-pool shares for $1,000 [F0012], the banner urges registration through the video link [F0001], and the presenter describes daily Bitcoin withdrawals as convenient for an investor [ASR_0002]. The later account view attributes commissions to team members [F0058]. Showing how to withdraw from an account does not resolve the risk in promoting share-based returns and team-linked earnings.

citations.quote: withdrawal is possible, every day, and withdrawal occurs in Bitcoins, as well as transfer reporting occurs in Bitcoins, which is very convenient for the investor.

opening.argument: The visible commercial proposition should be assessed for what it shows, not for additional terms a judge might infer. The site advertises GPU mining-pool shares with a displayed $1,000 purchase button [F0012], and its wallet history includes entries described as mining earnings alongside team-member commissions [F0058]. That is evidence of an offer and a commission structure, not evidence in these frames of how members joined or what anyone was promised to recruit them. The withdrawal page states a fee threshold and possible processing delay [F0018]. Even the accompanying link's destination is not shown; the description only says it offers information about earning cryptocurrency [DESCRIPTION_0001]. The record supports scrutiny of an ordinary-looking service offer, but it leaves the alleged deceptive terms unestablished.

citations.quote: http://cryptobiz.site/start - learn how to earn in cryptocurrency safely and easily

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution correctly identifies a purchase offer [F0012] and a withdrawal request [ASR_0001]. But those facts do not show that a buyer must recruit others, that a particular return is guaranteed, or what the linked site asks visitors to do. The wallet's team commissions warrant attention [F0064]; their presence alone does not supply the missing recruitment terms. Likewise, the unclear $50 remark cannot establish the terms of the displayed $1,000 share offer.

citations.quote: And here I just add a sum amount of 2.1 bitcoin.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: No unseen recruitment rule needs to be invented. The displayed offer ties a $1,000 share purchase to a GPU mining pool [F0012]; the account history describes mining earnings from shares and percentage commissions from members in the account holder's team [F0058]. The banner calls for viewers to register using the link below the video [F0001], while the presenter points to another imminent passive-income payment [ASR_0002]. A disclosed fee threshold does not change the character of that combined investment-and-earnings promotion.

citations.quote: the next fee for passive income as I had just mentioned is in just 20 hours everyday
